narrative.overview:
A purpose-built messaging operations center that combines the familiar comfort of a chat interface with the precision and clarity of a control panel. The dashboard is an extension of WhatsApp itself — the same conversations, the same parents, the same urgency — but elevated into a workspace where school staff have full operational visibility and control. Every pixel serves the operator: status is visible at a glance, conversations are one click away, and the system communicates its state without requiring interpretation.

The visual personality is bold and energetic with digital teal-blue as its signature, but disciplined in where that energy lives. Color is concentrated in status signals and primary actions; the surrounding workspace stays neutral and precise so the content — conversations, tickets, numbers — commands attention. The system borrows the rounded, card-based language of modern messaging apps but applies it with the rigor of an operations tool.

Interaction is tactile and responsive. Surfaces lift on hover, buttons acknowledge clicks, and state changes are animated. At rest, the interface is clean and flat; on interaction, it comes alive with subtle elevation and confident color shifts.
keyCharacteristics: Messaging-native: card-based conversation list, chat-bubble message view, WhatsApp-style delivery indicators
Status-driven: semantic color coding for every state immediately visible
Operationally flat: minimal decoration, maximum information density
Bold brand accent: digital teal-blue concentrated on primary actions and active states
Responsive shell: sidebar collapses to overlay on mobile, tables scroll horizontally

rules.name: The Status Palette Rule
rules.body: Every operational state maps to exactly one color pair. No state exists without a color assignment in StatusBadge.

rules.name: The Brand Concentration Rule
rules.body: Digital Teal-Blue appears only on interactive elements and the brand mark. Never on passive containers or backgrounds.

rules.name: The 14px Floor Rule
rules.body: Body text is never smaller than 14px. Labels and metadata go to 12px. Nothing below 12px except supplementary chart labels.

rules.name: The Lift-on-Hover Rule
rules.body: Cards are flat at rest (border only). On hover: border color shift and optional background tint. Shadows only for truly elevated surfaces.

rules.name: The No Double-Border Rule
rules.body: Adjacent containers sharing an edge use divide-y or a single shared border. Two borders touching creates a 2px seam that looks accidental.

dos: Do use the StatusBadge component for every operational state. Never apply status colors manually.
Do use .input and .btn-* component classes from index.css as the single source of truth.
Do use font-mono text-xs for machine-generated identifiers.
Do use the timeAgo() pattern for conversation timestamps.
Do provide empty states with centered gray-400 italic text inside the same card container.
Do use rounded-xl for page-level containers and rounded-lg for interactive elements within them.
Do use the lg: breakpoint (1024px) as the primary responsive threshold.
donts: Don't apply brand-600 to non-interactive surfaces.
Don't use shadows on cards at rest.
Don't mix badge styles — every status maps to exactly one StatusBadge color.
Don't create new button variants without adding them to the .btn-* family in index.css.
Don't use gray-300 text. The lightest readable text is gray-400.
Don't place content in a scrollable container without visible overflow indicators.
